title: $5.75 billion to back the founders building what’s next
gist: Bessemer Venture Partners raised $5.75 billion in a single close ($1.75B for seed/early-stage, $4B for growth) to keep backing AI-native founders across the full stack, and explicitly maps its new bets (DriveNets, fal, Fireworks, ClickHouse, EliseAI, Waymo, Saronic) onto pattern-recognition carried over from past investments (Mellanox, Twilio/Auth0, Toast/ServiceTitan/Procore, Rocket Lab).

insights.claim: Bessemer raised $5.75 billion in new capital in a single close, split into $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and $4 billion for growth investing.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A dedicated $4B growth pool signals BVP will compete more aggressively for late-stage and pre-IPO AI rounds, adding a well-capitalized bidder to that market.
insights.quote: we're announcing $5.75 billion in new capital to continue that work amidst this AI era: $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and $4 billion for growth, raised in a single close.

insights.claim: Roughly 70 percent of Bessemer's investments are made at the early stage, meaning the firm's deal volume still skews heavily seed/early despite the large growth fund.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: The $4B growth pool likely funds fewer, larger, more concentrated bets rather than broad-based late-stage deployment, so watch for outsized checks in a small number of AI winners.
insights.quote: Roughly 70 percent of our investments are made at the early stage.

insights.claim: Bessemer's growth investing has evolved from simply doubling down on its own early-stage winners into a standalone engine with a dedicated team that leads concentrated growth bets in top companies regardless of whether they started in Bessemer's portfolio.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: BVP is now an active outside bidder for growth-stage AI deals it did not originate, expanding the competitive set founders and co-investors should expect at late-stage AI financings.
insights.locator: Our growth strategy began as doubling down

insights.claim: Since 2022, Bessemer has backed more than 260 AI-native companies and invested over $3 billion across the full AI stack, spanning compute and infrastructure, foundation models, developer platforms, and AI applications/agents.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete benchmark (260+ companies, $3B+) for BVP's AI deployment pace since the post-ChatGPT inflection, useful for comparing against peer VC AI exposure.
insights.quote: Since 2022, we've backed 260+ AI-native companies – investing more than $3 billion across the full stack

insights.claim: Bessemer frames AI as creating value faster than any prior technology paradigm shift and as having already become the central nervous system across every sector of the economy, justifying capital deployment across the entire AI stack rather than a single layer.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Supports a thesis that AI investment broadens beyond compute/infrastructure into every vertical, arguing against a narrowing of AI capital to infra-only plays.
insights.quote: AI is creating more value, faster than any previous paradigm shift, and has quickly established itself as the central nervous system across every sector of the economy.
insights.locator: There's no question that the moment

themes.theme: Pattern recognition reused across tech cycles

insights.claim: Bessemer's networking-fabric investment in Mellanox (whose technology now connects GPU clusters powering modern AI) directly informed its later investment in DriveNets, and its earlier API-platform lessons from Twilio and Auth0 led it to back fal, Fireworks, and ClickHouse as infrastructure 'picks and shovels' of the AI build-out.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Bessemer explicitly reuses prior infrastructure and API-platform pattern recognition to source new AI infra bets, a repeatable signal for predicting its next networking/dev-platform investments.
insights.quote: Twilio and Auth0 taught us what turns an API into a platform; that's why we backed fal, Fireworks and ClickHouse as the picks and shovels of the AI build-out.
insights.locator: We backed Mellanox, whose networking fabric

insights.claim: Board experience at vertical SaaS leaders Toast, ServiceTitan, and Procore taught Bessemer where traditional software hits its ceiling, and that same pattern recognition led it to back EliseAI, EvenUp, and Legora as AI-native products breaking through where legacy vertical software stalled.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Signals BVP is actively hunting for AI-native disruptors of legacy vertical SaaS incumbents in its own past portfolio (e.g., healthcare, legal, insurance ops), a sourcing pattern investors can track for future deal flow.
insights.locator: Years on the boards of Toast, ServiceTitan

insights.claim: Bessemer's deep-tech/hardware underwriting experience from Rocket Lab, where capital intensity and regulatory timelines had to be solved simultaneously, gave it the conviction to back Waymo and Saronic in defense tech and physical AI.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Marks defense tech and physical AI/robotics as a deliberate expansion category for BVP built on hardware-underwriting muscle, a category worth watching for its next moves.
insights.locator: investments in deep tech and hardware like Rocket Lab
